title: Charged-replica symmetry-resolved Renyi-2
difficulty_explanation: The solver must preserve a global U(1) charge under complex hopping gates, prepare two implicit replicas of a 72-qubit TensorCircuit MPS, contract a seed-scrambled noncontiguous swap/charge pattern, and invert a shifted Fourier grid with the correct sign and sector normalization. Dense simulation requires 2^72 complex amplitudes per replica.
solution_explanation: The expert prepares the exact fixed-charge state with TensorCircuit MPSCircuit, reads its public MPS tensors, evaluates one- and two-replica transfer networks using the TensorCircuit backend, performs the declared shifted DFT, and computes normalized sector Renyi-2 entropies.
verification_explanation: The evaluator never imports TensorCircuit. It independently implements complex128 canonical NumPy TEBD and explicit one-/two-replica transfers, validates them against a separately evolved dense six-qubit reduced density matrix, and checks both oracle agreement and Fourier/normalization identities.
relevant_experience: This prototype combines fixed-charge circuit design, exact MPS gauge motion, replica permutation observables, charged generating functions, and shifted finite-group Fourier reconstruction.

contract.determinism_scope: Exact case bytes are bound by the pinned image/runtime and evaluator-emitted case_digest; a seed alone is not a cross-NumPy case identity.
contract.case_seed_source: verifier-only ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED, legacy ORBIT_RENYI_SEED fallback, or evaluator --seed
contract.hidden_holdout_status: pending; published seeds are validation canaries and are not private model-trial holdouts
contract.anti_hardcoding: The seed changes both fixed-charge input strings, complex hopping and interaction angles, subsystem masks and ordering, Fourier offsets, sector queries, and nonces. Oracle moments and entropies are not supplied.
contract.oracle: Independent NumPy canonical TEBD plus explicit one-/two-replica transfer networks and a separate dense reduced-density-matrix canary

seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: The single base seed initializes one NumPy Generator stream that emits both ordered fixed-charge replica cases.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: Exact public case bytes are deterministic under the pinned runtime and are identified by the evaluator-emitted case_digest.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted keys and compact separators over both ordered exact public cases; functional stdout emits the full case_digest and protocol_seed in one structured orbit_q_case_identity JSON line.
seed_protocol.pinned_numpy_note: The target image pins NumPy 2.2.6; a seed alone is not a cross-runtime case identity, so trial manifests must bind the image/runtime and case_digest.

difficulty_levers: 72 qubits rule out dense statevectors and 144-qubit explicit dense replicas
a scattered 24-site subsystem creates many swap boundaries and defeats a single-Schmidt-cut purity shortcut
complex U(1)-preserving hopping phases make basis and conjugation conventions observable
a per-case shifted 25-point Fourier grid tests transform sign, offset compensation, and charge labels
both unnormalized sector moments and normalized sector Renyi-2 values are scored
two cases generated sequentially from one verifier-only seed must share one deterministic implementation
claim_boundary: This is a deterministic synthetic fixed-charge circuit diagnostic, not an experimental randomized-measurement protocol. No solver-model trial has been run and no model-hardness claim is made.
admission_blockers: Freeze and independently record a private holdout seed schedule plus exact case_digest values before any solver-model trial.
Complete the authenticated full Harbor expert verifier and policy audit under the frozen trial image and resource envelope.
Human review must confirm the charged-moment convention, sector normalization, and framework-native replica contraction before promotion.
exploitability_risks: The evaluator source and completed validation seeds are public canaries; they cannot be reused as a private hardness holdout.

Because the entire circuit specification is public to run_solution, a standalone MPS implementation could reproduce the oracle; static and LLM policy audits must enforce that TensorCircuit prepares the state and performs the quantum tensor contraction.
numerical_statistical_risks: Fourier inversion can leave tiny imaginary or negative roundoff in weak sectors; the public validation minima are p(q)=2.189e-3 and Z2(q)=1.253e-7, and private holdouts still require prequalification.

The independent TEBD removes only relative-singular values below 2e-14 as numerical null directions; a pinned linear-algebra change that moves physical weight across this threshold requires revalidation.
Exact MPS ranks grow exponentially with brickwork depth despite the large qubit count; the four-layer profile is intentional and any depth increase requires fresh peak-memory and runtime profiling.
Sector Renyi-2 divides by p(q)^2, so low-weight sectors are excluded from queries and separately guarded by admission floors.
api_risks: MPSCircuit.apply_adjacent_double_gate must preserve the custom rank-4 gate tensor's output/input index convention.
MPSCircuit.get_tensors exposes the public MPS tensors but their gauge and center position are not fixed; the replica observable must remain gauge invariant.
MPSCircuit.normalize and the NumPy backend are process-global through TensorCircuit's backend/dtype settings.
backend.einsum contraction planning can change performance across TensorCircuit/NumPy versions; the pinned image and runtime margin must be revalidated after upgrades.
NumPy Generator byte-level cases can change across NumPy versions; manifests must bind case_digest and the pinned NumPy version.
